subject.title: feat: add hosted feed envelope verifier

question: Should OpenClaw accept this signed hosted-feed envelope verifier contract as the foundation for the hosted feed trust series before the linked RFC and follow-up slices land?
rationale: The code and proof are coherent, but automated review cannot decide the permanent signing context, payload typing, key-id matching, accepted key formats, or staged trust-boundary semantics.

options.title: Accept As Foundation After Review
options.body: Approve this primitive after confirming the verifier contract and merge ordering for config, refresh, persistence, and CLI visibility.

options.title: Hold For RFC Acceptance
options.body: Keep the PR open until the linked RFC direction is accepted, then re-review the implementation against the approved trust model.

options.title: Request Contract Hardening
options.body: Ask for narrower semantics or additional invariant tests before later PRs consume the verifier API.

recommendation.title: Accept As Foundation After Review
recommendation.body: Approve this primitive after confirming the verifier contract and merge ordering for config, refresh, persistence, and CLI visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work touches both the official external catalog and device-identity areas, making this the strongest available routing signal for a security-boundary decision.
